title: Subscriber reconstruction and verification playbook - delayed stream event
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a customer-facing communications draft and internal playbook for handling a delayed streaming/chunk delivery incident affecting a subset of hosted API tenants on 2027-03-15 UTC. It includes the short statuspage update copy, a plain-language postmortem summary for customers, suggested verification steps customers can run, and the evidence/attachment checklist we will publish.

Notes to self:
- Keep language plain, avoid technical jargon where possible.
- Two distinct outputs: 1) Status page short update (1-3 sentences), 2) Post-incident customer brief (short executive summary + timeline + actions).
- This is a draft for review by Eng SRE + Applied ML before publishing.

Statuspage short update (one-line + short detail):
Status: Degraded — Partial streaming delivery delays resolved
Updated 2027-03-16 04:30 UTC
Summary: We experienced delayed streaming/chunked responses for a subset of hosted API requests in eu-west-1 between 2027-03-15 02:10–03:28 UTC. Most requests were completed successfully after retries; a small percentage of sessions saw extended tail latency or truncated structured outputs. Full mitigation was applied at 03:28 UTC and we restored normal streaming behavior.

Suggested statuspage one-liner for customers:
"Partial streaming delays in eu-west-1; mitigated and routing restored. If you still see issues, contact support with request IDs."

Customer-facing post-incident brief (concise, plain-language):
Executive summary:
On 2027-03-15 at approximately 02:10 UTC we began seeing abnormal delays in streaming/chunked responses for a subset of requests routed to our eu-west-1 inference fleet. The issue caused extended per-request latency and in some cases truncated structured outputs or partial streaming artifacts. Mitigations were applied (automated routing fallback + cache flush + restart of a small number of serving workers) and normal service resumed by 03:28 UTC. No data was lost; all persisted tenant data and logs remained intact.

Impact:
- Affected tenants: approximately 4% of active tenants in eu-west-1 during the window (tenant IDs and counts available in evidence package).
- Symptoms observed by customers: delayed streaming responses (tokens arriving in larger batches), occasional truncated JSON in structured output, rare client-visible reconnects during long-lived streaming sessions.
- Duration: 02:10–03:28 UTC primary window; residual weakened tail up to 03:55 UTC for retries.
- Severity: moderate customer-facing impact for those using real-time streaming. Non-streaming generation and embeddings were largely unaffected.

Root cause (high level):
Short version: a recent autoscaling policy change plus an unexpected interaction with our streaming prefix cache eviction logic caused a small number of serving workers to accumulate large KV cache pointers without freeing memory. This increased throughput variance and delayed token emission for affected streams.
More detail for technical customers: during a controlled update to autoscaler thresholds (rollout queued via rollout-2027-03-15-A), a race condition surfaced between the cache-eviction gc job and the connection-handling loop when the system forwarded long-lived streaming sessions into warm-but-not-yet-ready workers. The workers accepted connections but were stalled while rebuilding large KV metadata, delaying the emission of token chunks until the KV state fully hydrated. The fallback routing that would normally avoid these workers was not triggered because the health probe returned healthy while the streaming emission path still blocked.

Immediate mitigations performed by Redwood:
- Activated automated fallback routing to healthy workers in additional regions for high-priority tenants (02:45 UTC).
- Issued a targeted restart of 12 serving workers with saturated KV pointers (03:02 UTC).
- Flushed prefix caches and added a guard to prevent KV state rebuilds on the hot path (03:12 UTC).
- Deployed a hotfix to autoscaler thresholds and gating logic (03:20 UTC).
- Reverted the aggressive rollout batch to the previous configuration to prevent recurrence (03:28 UTC).

Customer-facing actions and verification steps (what customers can do):
If you believe your requests were affected, please follow these steps to help us and to verify integrity of responses: 
1) Find representative request IDs or session IDs from your logs in the window 2027-03-15 02:00–04:00 UTC. Share them with support if you need help.
2) Re-run any critical streaming scenarios against the same model and prompt to confirm current normal behavior. Use a small sample of requests rather than full replay immediately.
3) If you rely on structured output (JSON, key-value extraction), validate key fields for truncation. If you find truncated objects, flag those request IDs to support.
4) For tenants using our SDKs: upgrade to SDK v1.12.3+ which includes improved reconnect handling and clearer client-side diagnostics.

Suggested customer message snippets (short):
- Short reassurance: "We observed a brief streaming delay in eu-west-1 on 2027-03-15. Impact was mitigated; please retry any affected requests or contact support with request IDs."
- Technical snippet for engineering teams: "If you saw delayed token arrival or truncated structured output, collect request IDs and share with support. Re-running against current endpoints should show normal streaming behavior."

Planned follow-ups / next steps (Redwood internal + customer-facing timeline):
- Short-term (next 48 hours): complete detailed RCA write-up, publish evidence package, notify tenants with confirmed impacts and offer assistive replay support.
- Medium-term (2 weeks): implement a permanent fix to decouple KV hydration from the streaming hot path and add a probe that verifies chunk emission latency rather than only connection health.
- Long-term (1–2 months): audit autoscaling rollout gating and extend chaos tests to include long-lived streaming session scenarios across all regions.

Evidence package to publish with customer brief (attachments we will include or provide on request):
- Per-tenant impact list (anonymized IDs available on request)
- Timeline of internal events and automated alerts (full logs for provided request IDs)
- List of worker IDs restarted and the exact configuration diffs rolled back
- Hotfix PR link and deployment tag (CONFLUENCE-1234 / PR https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/5421)

Escalation and support contact: 
- Primary CS contact: Marta Alvarez (marta@redwood.example) — customer recovery lead.
- Engineering contact for tenant verification: Devon Price (devon@redwood.example).
- Emergency on-call: SRE on-call channel #sre-incidents (include tenant request IDs when opening).

Open questions / follow-up items (internal):
- Need to confirm whether any third-party network appliance in eu-west-1 had TTL issues that correlated with worker kv-pointer growth.
- Validate whether the SDK reconnect telemetry needs expanding to show per-chunk latency in client logs.
- Decide whether to proactively offer credits or replay assistance for impacted enterprise customers (proposal due EOD 2027-03-17).

Draft customer email template (short):
Subject: Update on streaming delays in eu-west-1 on 2027-03-15
Hi <CustomerName>,
We wanted to let you know about a brief incident that affected streaming performance for a subset of requests in eu-west-1 on 2027-03-15. Our engineers identified a routing/cache interaction that caused delayed streaming token emission for some sessions. The issue was mitigated by 03:28 UTC and we have taken steps to prevent recurrence.
If you observed problems, please reply with representative request IDs and we will prioritize replay and verification for you.
Thanks for your patience — we’ll follow up with the full RCA and attachments within 48 hours.
— Avery Chen, Customer Recovery Lead

Checklist before publishing to customers:
- [ ] Engineering review of root cause text (confirm accuracy and no leaked internal-only details)
- [ ] SRE sign-off on timeline and worker restart list
- [ ] Legal/Trust review for any PII language (none expected)
- [ ] Regulated-customer outreach list compiled; schedule one-on-one calls where required
- [ ] Evidence package links created and validated

Revision history:
- 2027-03-15 initial draft by Avery Chen
- 2027-03-16 added engineering mitigation detail and contact list (Marta Alvarez, Devon Price)

End of doc.
